judge_assessment.explanation: The first hard failure is exact. Worksheet problem 4 reads 'Find the measure of angle F in degrees. (Which angle of triangle ABC corresponds to angle F?)' -- two printed responses, the measure and the correspondence -- and verify.json id 4 is a single solve '52+61+x-180' -> [67]. The correspondence (angle C) is nowhere in the file and the Quick Answers bank prints '4. 67' alone. The second hard failure is also supported: the directions state 'By CPCTC ... the two matched measures are equal. Write that equation first, then solve it' and 'Show the equation you solved', and problems 1 and 8(b) repeat it explicitly ('Write the equation CPCTC gives you', 'Write the correct equation and solve for x'); every verify entry records only the root. I would add one qualification the judge does not make: this sheet is the most disciplined multi-slot encoding in my batch. Ids 5, 6, 7 and 8 each carry one entry per lettered part, and 7 and 8 pair a manual entry for the open half with a solve entry for the computed half. So the second hard failure is a coverage gap in the sheet's weakest dimension, not a systemic absence of the technique -- problem 4 is the only item where a whole requested response is missing, and the equation slots are the one thing the author never modelled. All values recompute: x=5, y=15, x=8, 67 degrees, x=5 with 22 degrees, x=6 with AC=25, x=8, x=13. REJECT is correct.

strengths_to_preserve: The manual/computed pairing on problems 7 and 8 is the pattern the rest of this shard is missing, and it is here already. Problem 7 carries {"id": 7, "type": "manual"} for the two-column SAS proof AND {"id": 7, "type": "solve"} for the CPCTC algebra that follows it; problem 8 does the same for the correspondence diagnosis and its equation. Two entry kinds under one id, each covering a different printed slot.

Problem 8 is a well-built diagnostic: the congruence statement is deliberately scrambled (triangle ABC congruent to triangle DFE) so that the student who reads letters positionally gets AB paired with DF, and the student who pattern-matches alphabetically gets the wrong DE. Kim's stated error is exactly the misconception, and part (b) then makes the correct correspondence load-bearing in an equation.

Units are stated on every measured quantity and bound mechanically: centimetres, inches, metres and degrees appear in the stems, and verify.json carries answer_unit 'degrees' on id 5's eval and 'm' on id 6's eval, so check_answer_line.py ties them to the printed answer lines rather than leaving them as prose.

The value-free two-triangle reference figure with the caption 'How a congruence statement is read on this sheet: matching positions name matching parts. No values shown' fixes the labelling convention without giving any problem a figure that could be misapplied to its neighbour.

root_causes.description: Coverage is per problem id, so an item that already has one entry can print a second requested response with no gate objection. Problem 4 is the pure case: the id has a check, the check is right, and the parenthetical correspondence question is invisible to every gate in the chain.

root_causes.description: The correspondence equation the directions demand on every problem ('Write that equation first', 'Show the equation you solved') has no representable form. It is not a number, so no numeric type fits; it is not open reasoning either, since there is exactly one correct equation per item. With nothing to declare, the author declared nothing, and the requirement that appears in the directions of every problem is checked on none of them.

improvements.title: Problem 4's requested correspondence (angle C) is printed and unverified
improvements.proposed_change: Extend tests/check_layout.py to count printed response slots per \problem segment -- lettered parts, parenthetical follow-up questions ending in '?', \ansblank and \answerline -- and fail when that count exceeds the verify entries carrying that id. For this case, add a companion manual entry under id 4 declaring the expected correspondence ('angle C corresponds to angle F because C is third in ABC and F is third in DEF'), which also makes the Quick Answers bank show that something beyond 67 is being asked. The rest of this file already models the fix: ids 5, 6, 7 and 8 carry one entry per printed part.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem whose stem ends in a parenthetical question after the main instruction, with a single verify entry for its id; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming the uncovered slot. Exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the one whole-response gap on this sheet and generalises to every item that tacks a second question onto a computation. The requested response here is the sheet's declared focus -- correspondence -- so the gap sits exactly on the skill being assessed.
improvements.risk: Medium. Parenthetical questions are sometimes rhetorical scaffolding rather than a requested response; warn-only for a run and tune the pattern before making it a hard gate.

improvements.title: The CPCTC equation the directions require on every problem needs a declared manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Add to SKILL.md an explicit slot category for a required SETUP -- an equation, proportion or correspondence statement the student must write before computing -- and instruct that it be declared as a `manual` entry alongside the numeric check, with the expected setup in the `desc` so the answer key's grading note can be generated from it. Then have scripts/verify.py scan the directions block and each problem segment for setup imperatives ('write the equation', 'show the equation you solved', 'set up the proportion', 'write that equation first') and exit 2 naming ids that carry no manual entry. On curr-313 that fires on ids 1 through 6.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose directions read 'Write that equation first, then solve it' and whose problem 1 carries only a solve entry; assert verify.py exits 2 listing problem 1. It exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: The equation IS the CPCTC skill -- once it is written, the algebra is one line. Declaring it manual makes the trust boundary honest and gives the answer key a grading note for the half of the answer that carries the learning.
improvements.risk: Low-to-medium. Risks over-flagging sheets whose directions mention equations decoratively; exit 2 rather than exit 1 keeps the cost to one line of author review.

case_summary: This is the most disciplined verification encoding in my batch and it still fails, which is instructive. Ids 5, 6, 7 and 8 each carry one entry per printed part, and 7 and 8 correctly pair a manual entry for the open half (the two-column SAS proof, the correspondence diagnosis) with a solve entry for the computed half -- exactly the pattern the rest of this shard omits. The mathematics is right throughout (x=5, y=15, x=8, 67 degrees, x=5 with angle R = 22, x=6 with AC = 25, x=8, x=13), units are stated and machine-bound, and problem 8's deliberately scrambled statement (ABC congruent to DFE) is a sharp diagnostic. Two gaps remain: problem 4 asks 'Which angle of triangle ABC corresponds to angle F?' and only the 67 degrees is verified, and the correspondence equation that the directions demand on every problem ('Write that equation first', 'Show the equation you solved') is representable in no entry and checked on none. A smaller prompt note: the format asked for realistic applications, and only problem 6 (the bridge truss) supplies one.
